title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (cote 142, Galois action on Teichmüller). Γ is the arithmetic group (Galois group of K, or the arithmetic fundamental groupoid in which Γ acts). Π = π̂_1 of the geometric fibre. Θ is an automorphism (outer action on Π) of Γ, or of the arithmetic fundamental group/groupoid. The question, resumed from p.95, is when Θ lifts to an automorphism Θ̃ of a covering 𝒯̃ of the groupoid, given that Θ fixes a vertex x_0.

On this page Grothendieck drops the assumption that 𝒯̃ is connected.
- Geometrically, 𝒯̃ comes from a finite étale cover X'→X with X geometrically connected and X' only K-connected. That is, X' is connected as a K-scheme but its base change to K̄ may split into several components.
- Such a cover is encoded by the geometric fibre E_0 = X'_{x_0}. The arithmetic fundamental group acts transitively on E_0. Grothendieck writes it as 'Γ.Π_0', with Π_0 = π_1(X_{K̄}, x_0) = π_1(𝒯̃, x_0). With a rational base point this group is the semidirect product Π_0 ⋊ Γ.
- The geometric group Π_0 need not act transitively. Its orbits E_0/Π_0 = π_0(E_0) are the geometric connected components of X'.

The construction:
- (50): send each x' ∈ E_0 to its stabiliser Π_{x'} ⊂ Π_0. This map is Π_0-equivariant, with Π_0 acting on subgroups by conjugation.
- (51): passing to quotients gives π_0(E_0) → Σ = Ssgr(Π)/Π, the set of conjugacy classes of open subgroups. This sends each geometric component of X' to the isomorphism class of the cover of X_{K̄} it defines.
- Θ acts on Σ by transport of structure through its outer action on Π.

Necessary condition for lifting, finished on p.97:
- The image of (51) must be Θ-stable.
- More precisely, there must be a bijection π_0(E_0) → π_0(E_0) compatible with (51) and with the Θ-action on Σ. This is condition (52).

Conversely, any such bijection is induced by some Θ̃_0 : E_0 → E_0 that is compatible with the Π-action twisted by Θ (cf. (46)). Θ̃ is then determined by its values on one point per component.

This is the elementary Galois-category bookkeeping needed to extend the earlier lifting criterion from connected to non-geometrically-connected covers. It serves the problem of characterising which outer automorphisms of π̂_1 come from Γ (the anabelian / Grothendieck–Teichmüller programme).
errors: 'produit direct Γ.Π_0' is loose. The group acting on E_0 is the arithmetic fundamental group, an extension of Γ by Π_0. It is a semidirect product when x_0 is rational, not a direct product in general.

Stability of the image of (51) under Θ is weaker than condition (52), because (51) need not be injective: distinct geometric components can give conjugate subgroups. Grothendieck corrects this himself on p.97 by requiring a compatible bijection of π_0(E_0).

ideas.what: Describing a K-connected but not geometrically connected finite étale cover by its geometric fibre with a transitive action of the arithmetic π_1 and non-transitive action of the geometric π_1
ideas.modern_name: Galois correspondence for finite étale covers; homotopy exact sequence 1→π_1(X_{K̄})→π_1(X)→Gal(K̄/K)→1

ideas.what: Map from fibre to stabilisers, descending to geometric components → conjugacy classes of open subgroups, with Θ acting by transport of structure
ideas.modern_name: Equivariance of Out(π̂_1) on the set of conjugacy classes of open subgroups (isomorphism classes of connected covers)

ideas.what: Necessary and sufficient criterion for lifting a Θ fixing a base vertex to a non-connected covering of the groupoid: a bijection on π_0 compatible with the class map
ideas.modern_name: Lifting automorphisms along coverings of profinite groupoids

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine Galois-category bookkeeping: extending a lifting criterion to non-geometrically-connected covers. It is part of the known anabelian / GT programme of the late 1970s–80s, and contains no new result or unexpected connection.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: likely 'mais je ne suppose plus/pas maintenant 𝒯̃ connexe'.
'ce qui se signifie' is likely 'ce qui se traduit' or 'ce qui signifie'.
'en termes géométriques' should probably read 'en termes galoisiens/groupiques par E_0 = X'_{x_0}'. The image reading is uncertain.
The annotation under (51) reads roughly 'i.e. l'ens. des Π_0-orbites dans E_0', followed by an unclear remark about Π-ensembles.
'Remarquons qu'ici' is plausibly correct; the struck-out word before it is likely 'Ex'.
